[[File:DecipherCon 2002 Day 1A Terwilliger and Velasco.jpg|thumb|right|260px|Mitch Velasco at the [[2002 World Championship]].]]
'''Mitch Velasco''' (handle '''BartmanMLV''') was a Decipher-era [[Squadron Members|Squadron Member]], listed as Bravo 30 from Jacksonville, Fl. The slot was retired after Decipher's SWCCG run.

Decipher recruited volunteer Squadron Members in the 1990s to promote SWCCG locally (tournaments, demos, player support).

The Players Committee introduced him on 4 November 2003 as its new Player Advocate for Tournaments, "of Jacksonville, FL", after the departure of [[Andrew Howard]]; [[Josh Radke]] was to work full time with him on organized play.<ref name="pc-int0312" /> His introduction signs him as SWCCG Player Advocate for Tournaments, Bravo 30 and [[Shadow Squadron|Shadow 30]], of Jacksonville, Florida, in the Dagobah region, under the handle BartmanMLV.<ref name="velasco" /> It gives this major tournament experience:<ref name="velasco" />
* Florida State SWCCG Championship Open 2003
* [[DecipherCon 2002]] SWCCG SE Sealed
* [[DecipherCon 2002]] SWCCG Secret Squirrel
* [[DecipherCon 2002]] SWCCG New Hope Theme tourney
* LOTR North Florida Territorial Open 2002
* Florida ConQuest SWCCG Open 2002
* Megacon SWCCG Open 2002
* GameFest Jacksonville 2001
* GrailQuest 1999-2001
* Game Invasion 2001
* SWCCG Miami Open &amp; Bounty Hunter Tourneys 2001
* Florida Grand Slam SWCCG 2000
* DecipherCon Japanese Sealed Deck SWCCG 2000
* DecipherCon Young Jedi Worlds Day 1

== 2002 ==

In March 2002 MaryGail Coffee named Velasco as the Jacksonville squadron member who would teach the ''Austin Powers'' CCG at the Conquest convention in Kissimmee, Florida.<ref name="rfd119">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=8KvLjZofZcY&t=715s Broadcast 119 - Radio Free Decipher (15 March, 2002): Chris and MaryGail Coffee on SWCCG Open], Player's Council, YouTube (uploaded 13 May 2022), at 11:55. Preserved copy: [https://archive.org/details/youtube-8KvLjZofZcY Internet Archive]. Transcript: [[Radio Free Decipher/Episode 119 transcript]].</ref> Conquest hosted the first SWCCG Open sanctioned by the [[Players Committee]].<ref name="rfd119" />
